entries.reason: One test honestly answers two atoms and can wear only one label. C13-RUN-EXPLICIT-MIGRATION owns the title because the case is built around an explicit pin migration: it asserts the migration commit records from and to, that the old Turn keeps the current pins while the descendant adopts the exact new pins, and that both survive a restart from the storage snapshot. C13-ADV-UNEQUAL-PIN-MERGE is answered inside the same fixture at adversarial.test.ts:805-822, where a merge commit is constructed over parents that carry unequal pins and mergeRun rejects it with the equal-pinned error. That rejection needs the migrated pin divergence the surrounding case sets up, so splitting it into a separate test would rebuild the same seven-step fixture to assert one throw. The shared witness is a fixture cost, not a missing test: neither atom is verified by the other's assertions.
